concepts.def: Total momentum stays the same in a closed system

walkthroughs.body_html:
p = m × v

A 1500 kg car at 20 m/s has momentum 30 000 kg·m/s. That's a lot of oomph. 🚗

Momentum is a vector — direction matters.

A force acting over time changes momentum. F × t = Δp (impulse).

Rearrange: F = Δp ÷ t. That's Newton's 2nd law in full.

Crumple zones and airbags increase t in a crash, so F on the passenger is smaller. Safer! 🛡️

In a closed system: total momentum before = total momentum after.

A 2 kg trolley at 3 m/s hits a stationary 1 kg trolley and they stick. Before: 6 kg·m/s. After: 3 kg × v. So v = 2 m/s.

Useful for collisions, explosions, and recoil.
